findings.source_passage: Other poets have warbled the praises of the soft eye of the antelope, and the lovely plumage of the bird that never alights
findings.why_it_matters: The original's specific phrasing—'warbled the praises of the soft eye' and 'lovely plumage'—carries the mock-heroic register of the opening; the draft compresses to 'warbled the antelope's eye' and drops 'lovely plumage,' flattening the rhetorical posture.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'the praises of the soft eye of the antelope, and the lovely plumage of the bird that never alights' verbatim; the full phrase establishes the chapter's satirical-celebratory tone.

findings.source_passage: Thou shalt see my back parts, my tail, he seems to say, but my face shall not be seen. But I cannot completely make out his back parts
findings.why_it_matters: The biblical echo ('Thou shalt see my back parts') is a famous interpretive crux—Melville's allusion to Exodus 33:23 and the unknowability of God/the whale. The draft drops 'completely' from 'I cannot completely make out his back parts,' slightly weakening the qualifier that makes the epistemological joke work.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'I cannot completely make out his back parts' verbatim; the word 'completely' is load-bearing for the ironic modesty of the claim.

findings.source_passage: if he feel but a sailor's whisker, woe to that sailor, whiskers and all. What tenderness there is in that preliminary touch!
findings.why_it_matters: The draft renders 'feel but a sailor's whisker—woe to whiskers and all,' omitting 'woe to that sailor' and cutting entirely 'What tenderness there is in that preliminary touch!'—a rhythmically and tonally distinctive sentence that caps the irony of the passage.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'What tenderness there is in that preliminary touch!' after the whisker clause; this brief sentence is essential to the comic-sublime irony of the third motion.

findings.source_passage: Had this tail any prehensile power, I should straightway bethink me of Darmonodes' elephant that so frequented the flower-market, and with low salutations presented nosegays to damsels
findings.source_locator: Third motion (sweeping), second half of paragraph
findings.why_it_matters: The Darmonodes digression and the second elephant anecdote (extracting darts from a wound) are characteristic Melvillean erudite-playful asides; their absence thins the voice materially, though they fall below the highest signature tier.
findings.suggested_fix: If word budget allows, restore at least the Darmonodes' flower-market sentence to preserve the digressive voice texture of the third motion section.

summary: The draft preserves the major signatures with reasonable fidelity—including the Satan/Baltic/Dantean/Isaiah passage, the Hercules/Goethe/Angelo paragraph, and the closing Exodus allusion—but exhibits light voice flattening in the opening clause, a missing 'completely' in the interpretive closing line, and excision of the 'What tenderness there is in that preliminary touch!' sentence; none rises to high severity individually, and the total finding count stays below the regeneration threshold.
